briefNote: Three streams, held separately. The client is described by a deficit, not a topic. Topic-similarity matching returns peers, and peers have already solved their own version of it. A qualifier link replaces the pitch: the tool routes, the quiz sorts.

icps.name: Client · Founder in transition
icps.note: The form that carried them has ended and they know it before anyone else does. Income runs on their own name, or the next thing is being born under their hands. Three or four real things going and no sentence that makes them one thing. They do not look impressive on a profile. They look stuck. That is the signal. Do not pitch. Route to the quiz.

icps.name: Sweet spot · Practitioners who serve founders
icps.note: Coaches, studio operators, accelerator leads, community builders, agency founders who have done the work on themselves. Peers and partners, never prospects. The screening question decides everything: ask what they uniquely bring. A process answer means not ready. A who-they-are answer means ready. One yes here carries the method to a whole client base. The complementary shape wanted most is the grounded builder-operator, closer to execution and ordinary business physics.

icps.name: Altitude · Studio & program operators
icps.note: Running a venture studio, accelerator, or founder program successfully, and conscious about how they run it. Not a session. The technology, the platform, the frameworks, the investment thesis. Rare, and mostly already known. Flag one when it appears.

exclusions.label: builds their own typology system
exclusions.pattern: typology|psychometric|personality (test|system|profil|assessment)|human design|enneagram|\bmbti\b|16personalities|astrolog|archetype system|profiling system|assessment tool|categorization system|talent assessment
exclusions.note: Day 167, Yulia Winslow. The closest match on topic and structurally unable to buy: their premise is that self-report is unreliable, which is the premise the whole offer rests on.

Hi {first},

I work with founders in the stretch between the thing that has ended and the thing that has not started yet.

If that is where you are, there is a short quiz that sorts it honestly: findyourtoptalent.com/quiz. If it is not your problem, it says so and stops.

No pitch either way.

— Sasha

Hi {first},

I work with founders in the stretch between the thing that has ended and the thing that has not started yet. The line I hear most often is "I have several things going and I can't tell if they're one thing."

If that lands, there is a short quiz that sorts it honestly: findyourtoptalent.com/quiz. If it is not your problem, it says so and stops.

No pitch either way.

— Sasha
templates.practitioner_partners:
Hi {first},

You work with founders[[company: at {company}]], and it reads like you have done your own version of the work rather than only teaching it.

I build the layer underneath that: helping a person name the one thing they are uniquely best at, precisely enough to build a business on.

One question I ask everyone in this line of work, and I am genuinely curious about your answer: what do you uniquely bring, apart from your method?

Comparing notes, not selling anything.

— Sasha
templates.operators_at_altitude:

Running a founder program well is rare. Running it consciously is rarer[[company:, and {company} reads that way]].

What I bring sits underneath the program: an instrument for reading a founder's uniqueness, the platform it runs on, and the frameworks and thesis around it.

Worth a conversation at that level?

— Sasha
